utterances.text: In connection with the question of snipers at Ahmici, no conclusions whatsoever were reached by you, or your team, or the people to whom you spoke regarding the presence of snipers on the morning of April the 16th; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I'm not really sure, actually. If you could repeat the question, please, because it's -- the way it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's all right. Obviously, it was a poorly-phrased question. You never actually concluded anything with regard to the presence or absence of snipers in Ahmici on the morning of April the 16th, 1993, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You also paid a visit to the village of Miletici, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Are you aware of any investigations having been done into the terrible events that occurred in that village, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No, but we tried to report on that, on what we saw there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You're not aware of any punitive acts or any punishment being meted out to the people that were responsible for that massacre, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Or of any military officers being relieved of responsibility as a result of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's fair to say, sir, is it not, that during all of the interviews that you conducted in the city of Zenica, you cannot recall Mr. Kordic's name ever coming up once; that's fair to say, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is fair to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, in the briefing that you received from the British Battalion, your briefing was that Mr. Kordic was a politician, the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You weren't ever told that he was ever any kind of a military commander, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, you were briefed to the contrary, that Colonel Blaskic was the overall military commander of all HVO military forces in the Lasva Valley; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that that would be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In connection with the draft report that you prepared, sir, Exhibit D66/1, you say that there were 101 confirmed dead as a result of your fact-finding mission, 96 Muslims and 5 Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I don't know if we actually said "confirmed dead." I believe that we did try to confirm the list, the original list that was submitted to us to the best of our ability, and with all the information gathered, that that number was approximately accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. That's fair enough. You never saw any videotapes of Mr. Kordic, for example, giving press conferences, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You've never read any articles that summarise speeches given by Mr. Kordic, have you, or at least before you prepared this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I have since, yes. That is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you'd never seen any videotapes of speeches given by Mr. Kordic, other than in press conferences, if there were any, before you wrote your report, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, insofar as Mr. Kordic is concerned, you basically had no information yourself at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you very much, indeed, Witness AB.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness AB. My name is Goran Mikulicic, and in this case, together with my colleague, Mr. Kovacic, I represent the second accused, Mr. Mario Cerkez. I'm sorry to have my view obstructed like this but this is for security reasons, obviously. Witness AB, you stated that in the Zenica cinema hall, you had spoken with persons who had been accommodated there after the events in Ahmici and who were still in a state of shock. In relation to that, I would like to ask a couple of questions. You spoke with two women and you recorded those conversations, and you have also described their fate today. One of them, Mrs. Sadeta Ahmic, was asked by you to give you names of perpetrators, to the best of her knowledge, perpetrators of the crimes in Ahmici. Did she actually do that? Did she give you any names? Do you have any recollection of that today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't necessarily recall actually asking that question per se. I think that -- it's difficult to answer the question the way it was phrased. If you can just be a bit more specific. I believe that she did mention names, but with that particular person, I believe that she basically spoke into the tape recorder and that was just a small piece of information that I -- I'm not really clear, if you could rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It was entirely my mistake. I will try to be as brief as possible in my questions. But let us first establish something as a preliminary matter. As an official of the United Nations who worked in the service of human rights, you did not go to Ahmici in order to investigate individual responsibility of possible perpetrators; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your main task was to establish whether there had been any violation of human rights, and if so to what extent, and whether the authorities in Vitez and in that area could be possibly held accountable for that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Therefore, would it be right to conclude that you did not go there in order to identify the perpetrators of the crime as individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: However, while speaking to the persons in the Zenica cinema hall, to your best recollection, those persons, and I have three persons in mind, Mrs. Puscul, Mrs. Ahmic, and Mr. Ahmic, did give you certain indications as to who the perpetrators had been; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct, but also I did not speak to Mr. Ahmic at the cinema, it was at a different location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I understand. Is it correct, since you've mentioned Mr. Ahmic, that he said that he had recognised individuals who had been there that morning in the attack on Ahmici and that he had recognised them as his neighbours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: On the other hand, Mrs. Puscul also named certain individuals whose names can be found on the list that you have just been presented with; is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I have a question in relation to your arrival in Ahmici and the fact that you mentioned a certain flag that you had found there. Is it correct that it was a green flag with some Arabic inscription on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know by any chance anything about that particular type of flag? Was that an official flag that was used at that time in the area or was it some different flag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I'm not really clear. I don't believe that -- it is an official flag. I don't know if it was there officially.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you think, and is it your statement, that the official flag in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina was a flag with an Arabic inscription on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No, no, no, I didn't mean that at all. I've seen that flag before, but its presence in that area and why it was there, it was not an official flag of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection, Witness AB, as to the circumstances in which you had seen that type of flag before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: There wasn't much left of that particular flag, but I have seen -- I have seen that in, oh, I don't know, newspapers or in areas. I mean, I've seen the flag before. I really couldn't tell you exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to show the witness Z942 which has just been tendered into evidence so we can use it as the basis for several questions. I'm referring to the report with the attachments that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, it is coming up to 1.00. If you're going to embark on another area, are you going to be more than a few minutes or would it be more convenient to adjourn now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I think it's better to pause now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now, we'll take the break. Before we do, I want to mention something about Thursday's Status Conference. We have to plan the work of the Trial Chamber for the year, and in order to do that, we need to know how long this case is going to take because there are other cases, as you know, which the Trial Chamber has to deal with and it's a question of fixing dates for them. Now, the Prosecution, I hope, will be able to give us a clear indication of a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So far we haven't called on the Defence for any information, I think, but the time is coming when that's going to happen. It would be helpful to know an estimate, you won't be held to it, of course, but an estimate as to how long it is anticipated that the Defence might take, how long they would require. I know you can't estimate the length of cross-examination and that sort of thing, but it's a normal thing for counsel to give us an estimate of how long they think their cases may take. So we would be grateful on Thursday if that can be done so that we can plan for the rest of the year. Half past two, please. Could you be back then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With your permission, Mr. Naumovski and myself have changed places for better communication with the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness AB. I will keep you for a very brief time, with a few questions linked to these lists that we have already referred to. For that purpose, I should like to ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit 942, which was tendered today. Would you be kind enough, Witness AB, to open the document and the section referring to the list of victims in Ahmici. More than 100 names are on that list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe there may be confusion here. I may be able to resolve it. 942 was, I think, the interim report and did not come with any attachments. The witness is being examined on some attachments, both the lists which were shown to him by Mr. Sayers and a record of interviews that he had. I was going to put these documents in in re-examination in any event because it seemed that they would probably be helpful. We've given them the number 788, and if that would help Mr. Mikulicic, then he could have that as a document, and I'm happy to be counted as the producer of it. The list he will find towards the end are what I propose might become Exhibit 888, not 788.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It hasn't yet been formally produced. May I hand in enough copies for the Chamber and the other defendant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Sorry for this confusion, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Witness AB, you have the document in front of you now, so will you please look at the document marked 0074648. That is the beginning of the list of names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I have a document which is listed 649. Oh, excuse me, yes, I do have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can the same be said of this document as what you said a moment ago, that you don't really know who gave it to you and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I'm not really sure exactly who gave me the document, but I'm fairly confident that I received this document in Zenica at the cinema building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This document was written in Croatian and the title was added in English. Can you explain? Was this something that you did or that was already indicated on the document when you received it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I can't recall, but I can tell you that this is not my handwriting. I did not write this on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's something which I have for the legal officer, please. Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to look at the document marked 0074653. It comes a little later in this batch. Would you say that this list was given to you by the same person as the previous one, if you can remember, of course?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I can tell you very clearly -- I haven't seen this in such a long time, but clearly it's my handwriting in between the above text and the bottom text where I write, "This is a list of war criminals." That is my handwriting. I did scratch that onto this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Witness AB, you envisaged what my next question would be. So the words in English in between the two paragraphs was written by you in the English language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In that case, can you perhaps recollect what prompted you to say that this was a list of war criminals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: If I recall, there was a difference between the lists, and I would have said, "Right, so what is this now," to the person who handed it to me, "What is this?" And at that time, they said, "Well, this is a list of the perpetrators," or something like that, to that effect, and then I would have just quickly written on top, which I obviously have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I see. Be so kind as to look at the previous list marked 00074654.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is very possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Witness AB, will you please examine a photograph that was tendered today into evidence and tell us whether, perhaps, on this photograph you can recognise the woman as the person we have just referred to? So could this photograph be placed on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Out of an abundance of caution, I wonder if that name is one that ought to be allowed to go out in public. I have no instructions to protect the name, but given the sensitivity of the matters that we are dealing with, I wonder if a source of information of that type ought to be redacted from the transcript, if possible, and asked about in a discreet way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: So the question, do I recognise the person from a photocopy of a photograph labelled D160/1, this one here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No, I don't believe that this is the person. I remember this lady being a little bit heavier set.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. That brings to an end my cross-examination, Your Honours. Thank you, Witness AB. [In English] Your Honour, if I might return on my place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May document Z888 be under seal for reasons of sensitivity, and I have, I think, two questions to ask the witness in re-examination, the first relating to Z888.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you'd just look at that document, please, Witness AB, that you've just been looking at, the typed pages that start at the bottom with 74639 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Are these working -- what are these? Because we can see that they are the documents on which you've been cross-examined as to interviews. Can you remember now what these typed sheets are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Well, there's actually -- there's a difference between the first two pages, 639 and 640 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I believe that this is where we tried to type up some of our notes. We weren't required to do this, but we believed that there would be an investigation, a proper criminal investigation that would be conducted, so we attempted to put it together. I know this because we added a number of footnotes which helped to verify --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Coming to the footnotes, as, indeed, I was --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- starting at 641, we can see your methods revealed in the footnotes where, for example, as item number 1, you visit a location and confirm something that's told to you, and if we turn over several pages, we can see similar entries, in particular, at 644, footnote 7 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- where a particularly nasty incident was spoken of and then confirmed by a finding of yours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Could you just, to complete the explanation to the Chamber, turn over two more pages. There's the map you've already spoken of, and then at 647 there's a hand-drawn plan. In case anybody wants to know what it was, what was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: This would have been one of the first from -- the first contacts or the first interviews that I had in the Zenica cinema. This would be a piece of paper that I presented to one of the witnesses to get an idea of the village, the location of that individual's home on a rough map because I didn't have a proper map, so to put into perspective where that individual lived versus the road and so on. This is what that served. If I might add one thing, if I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If it's on the point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: These documents are assembled here as an entirety; in fact, I can't recall ever -- these documents were all separate. They really were not compiled as a report and here they're presented as a report. The first two pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: They are not necessarily being presented as a report; they are simply being presented as documents provided by --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Right. Okay, but we never issued this as a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: These documents that we've just been looking at show something, in any event, of the notes that you made --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- and of the system that you were employing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've been asked questions about your experience and methods and so on. Do you stand by the report that you prepared with the other witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: The report that was submitted to Mr. Masowiecki?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's all I ask of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you for coming to give your evidence. You're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Before the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While we're preparing for the witness's departure, the next witness is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before we go on to the next witness, there may be a point about this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just one very minor point, Your Honours. It's on page 96, line 4 of the transcript. I'd just like to clear something up with the Trial Chamber's permission. The question was: Q You've never read any articles that summarise speeches given by Mr. Kordic, have you, or at least before you prepared this report?" And the answer says: A I have since, yes. That is accurate. I just want the record to be clear that the witness was agreeing with what I said, and that was that prior to preparing his report, he had not read any articles that summarised any speeches or consisted of speeches given by Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is that right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would like to take a seat. Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness, you have been asked for protective measures which have been granted; therefore, the pseudonym "AC" will be used in addressing you. But first of all I would like you to tell us whether this is, indeed, your name that is written on this document that will be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, that is my name as is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, paragraphs 4 to 7 of the summary submitted to you have to do with identifying information regarding the witness. So I would like to ask, if possible, for us to go into private session to deal with these paragraphs, 4 through 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness, we're going to cover the facts that occurred between the 18th and the 22nd of October, 1992 at the time when there was a conflict in Novi Travnik. You recall that on the 18th of October, 1992 a conflict broke out in Novi Travnik, and the next day, on the 19th of October, around 22.00, you attended a meeting at the headquarters of the Territorial Defence, a meeting at which the accused Mario Cerkez participated, as well as the mayor of Vitez, Ivan Santic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the course of that meeting, Mario Cerkez and Mr. Santic requested the Muslim representatives to allow free passage for forces coming from Busovaca to reinforce the troops stationed in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May I ask my colleague not to lead for the next three paragraphs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us about what Mr. Mario Cerkez and Mr. Santic said in the course of that meeting, and also what happened in the course of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: The meeting, as you said, was held on the 19th of October, 1992. Mr. Mario Cerkez, the accused, and Mr. Ivica Santic made an ultimatum to allow passage to HVO units from Busovaca to Novi Travnik to support HVO units which were in Novi Travnik. So the exclusive demand was to lift the blockade on the Busovaca-Vitez road at the section near Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the Muslim representatives, and I'm having in mind the military representatives of their delegation, to this request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Since it was an ultimatum, the representatives of the Muslim party were not willing to talk at that level about that specific problem. Fuad Kakjno, as one of the most prominent representatives of the Bosniaks in Vitez, suggested that the question should be debated during the following day. However, Cerkez and Santic insisted on their request, and they insisted that the blockade of the road be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Bearing in mind this refusal of the Bosnian representatives, what was the decision that Mario Cerkez took during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: During the meeting, faced with such a response of the Muslim side, Cerkez said that he had to consult with his boss, Mr. Kordic, who at that time was somewhere in the area of Novi Travnik. So he made a telephone call, and we could tell by that telephone conversation that Mr. Kordic was abiding by his ultimatum and that he was insisting that the road in Ahmici should be deblocked. At one point in time after that, sometime after that, Fuad Kakjno approached the telephone, and he also spoke to the accused, Mr. Kordic. And at that moment, we could hear -- from the receiver, we could hear Kordic, who said that there would be no negotiations until the ultimatum was respected, that there should be no talk, and that there was only one thing that could be done. Otherwise, we would not be responsible for what could follow. He requested that the BH army commander, Refik Lendo, be turned over to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did he speak about the commander of the BH army in Novi Travnik during that telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I did not get that answer in the French translation, and now that I'm looking at the transcript of the English interpretation, I can see that the witness has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Following that telephone conversation, there was a refusal by the Muslim side, and Mr. Cerkez and Mr. Santic withdrew at that point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. They withdrew and returned to the HVO headquarters. Half an hour later, approximately, they again called the Muslim representatives and again issued an ultimatum to the same effect, that the route be deblocked, since they did not get a satisfactory answer once again. Immediately after that, the location where they were was hit by a hand grenade, which fell a few centimetres -- a few dozens of centimetres from the entrance to the room, and one can conclude that the person who was targeting the building knew exactly who was in the building at that time and that the building was actually -- that representatives of the Muslim community were at the building at the time. However, the grenade did not hit its target, because it fell several centimetres away from the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You spoke about a new ultimatum which was conveyed by the telephone to Mario Cerkez and Ivan Santic. Was it said, during that ultimatum, that the village of Ahmici would come under attack if the blockade was not removed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what was said. Cerkez said that if the barricade is not removed, the village of Ahmici will come under attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: As regards this grenade that fell near the building, you don't know what the source of it was, you don't know where it had come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: I could not confirm anything, because -- although later on, there were rumours around the town as to the perpetrators of that act. However, there is no reliable information about that because no investigation was conducted later on, and I do not wish to accuse anyone for that attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the following day, on the 19th of October, which took place on the -- that is, in the morning of the 20th of October, the village of Ahmici was attacked, and you know that the attack had been conducted by the local commander of the Ahmici area. His name was Nenad Santic, and he was therefore responsible, in charge of the area of Ahmici, Zume, and Santici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: One of your cousins, your brother-in-law, to be precise, told you that Nenad Santic had personally used a grenade launcher and that he was the person who targeted the Ahmici mosque, who hit the minaret of the Ahmici mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. He was killed later on during the events in Ahmici. He lived in the immediate vicinity of Nenad Santic, the cousin of mine, and he had such information, and that was what he told me once.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 22nd of October, 1992, two days later, a ceasefire agreement was finally signed. I would like now to show you a document which has already been produced in this case, Exhibit number Z246. Witness, could you please tell us whether this document is the document which consists of the ceasefire agreement you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the document I referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The name of Mario Cerkez appears as the name of one of the signatories of this agreement, does it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. In early 1993, on the 26th of January, 1993, sometime after midnight, you were attacked at your home, you and your family, by HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. This took place on the 26th of January, after midnight. Two armed soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council forced their way into my apartment. They were asking for weapons, and they also wanted some other information. They abused me in front of my family. They maltreated members of my family. They also physically attacked me, and they spent some two hours at my place torturing all of us all the time. They took away all valuables, all money and jewellery which they could find at my place. But I happened to survive the attack. However, they spent the whole night in an orgy, those soldiers of the HVO, because later on, on the next day, we were informed that the same happened to about 20 other Muslim families in the same part of the town. I reported the event to the authorities of the Bosnian police. However, no investigation was ever conducted, of course, and I am not aware -- I do not know who the perpetrators of this criminal act were. However, what I can tell with certainty was that one of them was a local member of the HVO, because he was wearing a mask on his face, which indicated -- which testified, actually, to his desire not to be recognised. And aside from that, he spoke in such a way that it was possible for me to conclude that it was someone from the area, from the immediate vicinity. However, I cannot say exactly who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Sometime later on, on the 3rd of February, 1993, a murder was committed in the village of Nadioci. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am saying this for the benefit of the Defence, and I would like this to be excised from the transcript because the name of the witness could be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: A TV crew from the Vitez TV, where you worked at the time, was sent to film the scene of the crime. During that crime, the house of that person, of the victim, was also destroyed in an explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You have handed over to our office a videotape which is actually a documentary that was made at that time. You were able to view this tape during your interview yesterday with the representative of our office.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the material in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a videotape which was exhibited as Exhibit Z559, and it was used during the examination of another witness sometime earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness, you had some information according to which the perpetrator of the incident was an individual by the name of Miroslav Bralo, also known as Cicko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. That information was provided to me by my brother-in-law, my sister's husband, who lives in the immediate vicinity of that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Miroslav Bralo apparently bragged about being the perpetrator of that crime, according to the information you had at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you could say so, because -- the incident in question was a murder, and it would only be logical for a perpetrator to cover all the traces of the crime. However, this is not what happened in this case. The individual in question bragged about this on several occasions in the village where he lived at the time, and he also said that he had been the perpetrator of the crime to the members of the Bosniak community in the area. He said that he was the person who had killed the victim we spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You learned that there had been a meeting chaired by Mr. Pero Skopljak, who was the president of the Vitez HDZ. During that meeting, Mr. Skopljak suggested that a joint investigation should be conducted into the killing that had been committed, and according to your knowledge, the individual named Bralo was never a suspect in that investigation concerning this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. The individual -- the way the incident was -- the crime that was perpetrated was very cruel, and this, of course, caused tension in the area. You have to bear in mind the political activity of the authorities who were in power at that time in Vitez, and a meeting was held which was attended by Mr. Pero Skopljak, as a representative of the Croatian side, and he did promise an investigation into this incident, and he promised that adequate measures would be taken to punish this individual. However, no report was ever made on that investigation, and according to what I know, Miroslav Bralo was never indicted and was never punished in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During 1993, you yourself were arrested and detained. We shall speak about that later on. During your detention at the Kaonik camp, you heard the name of Miroslav Bralo mentioned again, and apparently a friend of yours who was digging trenches under the control and command of Miroslav Bralo on one occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. While I was in Koanik, that is, from the 5th until the 15th of May, 1993, I had contact with certain individuals who, because of their ethnicity, because of their Bosniak ethnicity, were detained there, and a person who had been taken to dig trenches told us that a certain individual nicknamed Cicko -- and this man was not from our area, he was not from the area of the Busovaca or Vitez municipality so he was not quite sure who the individual in question was. However, he remembered the nickname of Cicko, and he told us that he had bragged about killing a family, a whole family, that is, two families, families (redacted) and (redacted), in the village of Nadioci. Those people apparently lived in his neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Those two families were killed during the attack on Ahmici on the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, the incident took place on the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You personally knew Bralo. He could have been easily recognised by the authorities in Vitez because of the way he dressed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember him but not very well. I remember him from a period of time where he had no importance whatsoever in the municipality of Vitez, nobody was ever really interested in him. But what I remember was the very extravagant way he dressed, he always wanted to be somehow special, and that is why he stood apart from other people in that town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, Witness AC, the individual named Bralo belonged to the HVO in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I would like to show you a photograph which is marked Z1600.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photograph should be found in one of the new exhibits that have been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether the person you have mentioned, Miroslav Bralo, nicknamed Cicko, is the person on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A clarification for the record. Speaking of the videotape, it is the videotape exhibited 2559.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At the beginning of April 1993 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, I waited for my colleague to reach this paragraph. First of all, I would like to ask that everything related to Mr. Kordic be without leading questions. However, I have one additional objection, if you will permit me. In relation to paragraphs 42, 47, and 51, we do object because it calls for speculation or hearsay at least, although it could be termed as rumours as well, and there are no foundations whatsoever for these allegations. I believe that in respect of these paragraphs, Rule 89(D) should be applied because I believe that the need to ensure a fair trial outweighs the probative value and the quality of what is being discussed in these paragraphs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us if, at the beginning of April 1993, the accused Dario Kordic gave any statements in the media concerning the passage of the Bosnian army units in the territory under the control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the issue that was debated at that time, and this is what Kordic said in the media. This was also broadcast on the radio and television of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It had to do with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me interrupt the witness. Did you hear this, Witness AC, yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You did. Very well. Tell us what you heard said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: I heard in the media, and this was broadcast on the Bosnia-Herzegovinian television, that in the period around the 15th of April, in parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina which were predominantly Croat, units of the BH army were supposed to be placed under the command of the HV [as interpreted] units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So that the record can be clear, you referred to the HVO units and not the Croatian army units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said command of the HVO units. I just want the record to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness, what was the reaction of the BH authorities to that request which was made by Kordic in the media?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: There was no official reaction because this was not officially conveyed in any way, not in writing or in any other form, this ultimatum or this request, rather; however, the response of the Bosniak community and the leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina was such that it excluded all such possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Following that ultimatum that you referred to which was formulated by Dario Kordic, were there any incidents that took place as a result of that in the municipality of Vitez? Were there any arrests of Muslims, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: During the said period, because the ultimatum was running by the 15th of April, members of the BH army, it was clear, were not going to accept the ultimatum. So a few days before the 15th, a lot of pressure was exerted on the members of the Bosniak community, and those residents were arrested in the municipalities of Novi Travnik and Busovaca, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently, we do not have simultaneous interpretation anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. The witness should be asked to repeat the passage that has not been interpreted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: The ultimatum which the accused Kordic sent out and which was to be met by the 15th of April, 1993, as it was obvious that the members and the leadership of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina would reject such an ultimatum, for a few days before the expiration of the ultimatum, very forcible pressure was brought on individual Bosniaks, especially those who held prominent, eminent positions, eminent posts, among the Bosniak people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, the request for a meeting, was this formulated by the representatives of the Croats and put to the representatives of the Bosniak population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: The repression against the members of the Bosniak people was growing those days, and Bosniak representatives asked that a meeting be convened so as to try to solve the problems which were accumulating; however, representatives of the Croat side proposed that a meeting of such a nature and of such a level be held on the 16th of April, that is, the next day, around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You yourself were informed about the arrangement of that meeting by Muslim representatives in Vitez. Could you tell us who it was who told you about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: About the meeting and the outcome of the meeting, I was given information by the late Saban Mahmutovic and Sefkija Dzidic, who was the commander of the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The day set for the meeting, the 16th of April, it was the day when the HVO launched an attack on Vitez, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did this attack come as a surprise to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, to me personally and all the other members of the Bosniak people, all the more so as we expected, I could say, that a meeting would be held that day which would resolve the problems that had accumulated in the municipality of Vitez. May I also remind you that the massacre in Ahmici took place that morning at around 5.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Why did the HVO withdraw its proposal to hold this meeting and on that same day, that is, on the 16th of April, launch an attack on the village of Ahmici? Isn't that contradictory, calling a meeting and then conducting an attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Well, it could be a contradiction, unless we knew what would happen the next day. The butchery in Ahmici was a major tragedy which could not have happened just like that, which could not have been a spontaneous one. It showed that there was a well-organised plan behind it. Therefore, the proposal to hold a meeting that would be presumably held on the 16th of April was intended to undermine the vigilance, the alertness of the Muslim population and thus mask the attack on the members of the Bosniak people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You yourself met surviving refugees from the massacre in Ahmici. Did these persons speak to you about Nenad Santic who had, according to them, taken part in the massacre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything about the role that Nenad Santic played there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes. The survivors all testified that the operation was headed by Nenad Santic, that he was in one of the houses in Santici, and those who survived were taken for interrogation by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you get any information at the time about the Ahmici attack, about the attack on Ahmici in the area of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Go carefully and we'll hear what the evidence is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At the time that we are talking about, that is, April 1993 and in the days after that, did you get any information regarding the attack on Ahmici and the attacks launched by the HVO in the area of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: I and my family were in the town which was formerly controlled by the HVO, and our movement was restricted, that is, we could not leave that area. But I knew what had happened in Ahmici that very morning and I knew about the crimes committed by the HVO in the town, having killed seven civilians in the part of the town controlled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: According to the information that you could collect, some of it you also learned yourself, this attack had been prepared.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: No doubt, I think, one can claim with certainty that it was an organised and planned attack and that its launching and its preparation involved the highest ranking structures of the Croatian Defence Council, not only in Vitez but throughout the Lasva Valley. When I say that, I mean that the accused Kordic was the top-most military and political representative of the Croat people, that he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I must interrupt you, Witness AC. We do have our rules about evidence and we have to deal with it very carefully. Now, who told you about Kordic in this connection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: What I'm saying now is the result of my analysis which is, if I may call it that, an intellectual analysis, an analysis of a man who was present in the military and political life in the municipality of Vitez. In other words, Dario Kordic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. What we want to hear really is your evidence. Did you see Dario Kordic at all in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: That morning, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: At about this time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: No, I did not. No, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness AC, did you have a document in your possession or did anyone speak to you specifically about the responsibility of the accused Kordic for the events that you have just told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: I can only refer to a large number of people who thought about those things and who came to the same conclusions about the event as I did. But a document that would be charging the accused with the responsibility, no, I do not have such a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lopez-Terres, we shall not admit the evidence, 47 or 51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lopez-Terres, you should know in this case, and also whenever you're preparing some testimony, this objective, that individual analysis of various individuals simply are of no concern to us, individual analysis or impressions. We cannot use these impressions, and you should know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may draw attention to the fact that there is a second part of paragraph 47 which concerns another name, and that the witness has simply had no opportunity of telling us anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about a name for the operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And who did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: The first time that name -- 48 Hours of Ashes and Dust, the first time I heard it was at the time of my stay in the Kaonik prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And who told you that that was the name of the operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: It was a member of the BH army who had also been detained, and in the passages -- who had been detained before me and who even was in prison before the attack on Ahmici, that is, a man who at the time was not outside, and he mentioned that name. It meant nothing to me, because at that moment I knew nothing either. But when I came out, after I was exchanged, I was told that that name -- the name of that operation was also used by the intelligence of BH army from the detained HVO members at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The 18th of April, 1993, at the time where you were still at home, you heard a very powerful explosion which took place in Stari Vitez. Do you remember about half an hour before that explosion that you and your family and other inhabitants of the building were told -- were asked to seek refuge in the cellar of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. Since my family and I were in the part of the town controlled by the HVO and it was Sunday, the 18th of April, half an hour before that detonation an armed HVO member was going from one flat to another, warning the tenants to go down to the cellar. We did not have a clue as to what it was, so we simply blindly complied with that order. And when we reached the cellar, that is, my family and I, we saw already very many people there. About half an hour later, a terrible explosion took place. The size of that explosion, I can tell you that its aftermath was terrible, because even -- because we were about one kilometre from the site of the explosion, and nevertheless some of the window panes in our building were also shattered and broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness AC, that soldier who warned you about the imminence of that event, when he told you to go to the cellar, it was a local soldier from the Vitez Brigade, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: He was a local soldier and he had the HVO flashes, but one could not really say whether he was a member of the Vitez Brigade or not from those flashes. But since he was a local man, a man from that place, I believe that he indeed was its member.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On that same day, on the 18th of April, you were arrested and taken to the cinema in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us, who were the persons, or at least which units did the persons who arrested you belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: They were members of the HVO military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And those military policemen, were they the regional military police or the military police of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Those members were from Vitez, but I don't know the hierarchy or how those military police were organised. I don't know, but I believe it was the local military police which made part of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You were taken to the cinema. That cinema, was it far from the Central Bosnian headquarters in the Vitez Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: It was in the immediate vicinity, perhaps a couple of dozen of metres from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And was that cinema a place envisaged for the admission of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason for which you were incarcerated in that particular place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: The probable reason for which 600 Bosniaks were taken into custody and incarcerated in the cinema and the SDK and the chess club could be the fact that in this manner they prevented certain operations, that is, operations undertaken by the members of the BH army against the HVO units after the Ahmici massacre. That is, the real reason for which we were put there could be found in the fact that we served as a kind of a shield that was to protect that particular command. That is what I will say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the cinema, you tell us you found several hundred detainees. You were put in different precincts, in different rooms. There was the central -- the big central hall where the majority of prisoners were kept, and there were other places as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Which unit guarded the cinema, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: The members of the HVO military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I shall ask you once again the same question. Would you know if this was the military police?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I object now. It is the third time consecutively, and I was quiet. It is really more than leading a witness. Each time -- on the first question, he said, "HVO military police." Then on the second, he said, "Well, I'm thinking it may be," but it is the third time consecutively that he's led to say Viteska Brigade, not to mention that his summary, it was Viteska Brigade, which was not repeated on the normal reaction and first answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's ask the witness. Did you know, Witness AC, where these military policemen came from who guarded the cinema?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: I knew, because I knew some men. I know the full names of some of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And where was it they came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: From Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just an observation. To remind, I'm not really trying to lead the witness, to prompt the witness. And, secondly, my question was simply, "Do you know which unit guarded the cinema?" I wasn't prompting -- I wasn't leading the witness in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You said that you know some names, names of men of the unit who guarded the cinema. Could you give us those names, if you still remember them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. Those were men I knew well, and the name of one of them was Anto Kovac, nicknamed Sabac, and Zlatko Nakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now I should like to show you a document, Witness AC, Z591.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have objections on this document, and that is for several reasons. First, this document was not disclosed to the Defence, so we did not have any opportunity to check and to see about this document. Second and more important, there are no identifications on this document; like there is no number of the document, no date, no signature. We are not even sure whether it is a complete document. There's no stamps, which usually appear on HVO documents; very untypical by its format, letters, matters of numbering. And even on top of it, we can see added writing, handwriting, in the Dutch language. So for us, we would really ask the Prosecutor, if he wants to use this document as an authentic document, that it should be identified in the proper way. It is the first time we are raising the issue of authenticity, because this one is really out of appearance because of the reasons I've stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this document, as you can see, comes from the Vitez Brigade, to begin with. It is a list of 290 persons in that brigade. Why do we want to show it to the witness is to show that his name is on this list. As for the origin of -- as for the source of the document, as my learned friend has noted, yes, indeed, there is something in Dutch for the simple reason that this document was filed with the Office of the Prosecutor by a witness who already testified and who is an officer, Henk Morsink, a Dutchman who was with the European Mission. This document was submitted to us by Mr. Henk Morsink, and in view of the large number of documents which the witness Morsink could show to this Chamber, it's simply at the time of his testimony it did not seem particularly important to join a document containing a large number of Muslim names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, the document can be shown to the witness. He can be asked if he recognises his own name and, indeed, any others on the list as being people who were detained in the cinema. But he can't go any further than that in the way of producing it or authenticating it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness, this document is now being shown on the ELMO. Witness, do you recognise your name under 206 of the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And is that your date of birth and is that the name of your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you recognise any other names, especially 212?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, 212. And here, as you were talking, I was looking through it. I recognise quite a number of names, so for people who had been taken into custody together with me and then detained with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you, and we shall finish -- do you recognise the name 263?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: That is the name of Mr. Edib Zlotrg, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And 212, which you mentioned, it is the name of a person called Baktija Sivro, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, we never opposed the fact that those particular mentioned persons were there, and if I may remind the Prosecutor, there is already a document numbered D28/2 on which all the names he's just mentioning appear. So there is no need to try to show that this document is true in such an indirect way. It's simply not a true document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You dispute that this is an accurate document, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm disputing the document itself. Yes, these three or four names, yes, it is quite true, they were there, but we can see that from other documents, even from documents which the Defence produced. I think that now, in this way, by recognising some of the witnesses from this list of 299, yes, the witness will recognise five, six, or ten, and I think that it is an attempt to authenticate a document by introducing it at the back door, and we are against that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The fact is the witness is able to identify his own name on the list. He said, in general terms, that he could identify quite a number of the names, and he specifically identified three. We'll admit the document insofar as it goes, that he's identified those names. If the Prosecution want to call more evidence about it to authenticate it, that's a matter for them, but it's sufficient at this stage that it's identified in the way in which it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just -- in order to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lopez-Terres, I speak in my personal name, I do not quite understand what is the interest of this whole matter regarding this document. There are two elements that Mr. Kovacic has just referred to. Either you're producing the document to authenticate it as such and you told us that that was not your objective and, therefore, the document is not being produced as an authentic document as such, it is a document brought by a Dutch officer, as you have told us, but which had not been disclosed earlier on; or you're producing it to ask the witness to recognise his name. Maybe I'm not very lucid this afternoon, but I do not understand what is the point in producing a document to make the witness recognise his own name. Of course he knows his own name. Because what is the purpose of the document? That is the only basis on which we can discuss it. Otherwise, we're just looking in the dark. I don't quite know whether it will be well-translated. It means opening doors, leaving doors open regarding evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. You know, Your Honour, how difficult it is to produce documents coming from the Defence or, in any event, from the accused and the HVO, and it is difficult for the Office of the Prosecutor to reach people who could authenticate this list because we do not have many witnesses who are former members of the HVO, and the accused themselves have refused to testify in their own case. Therefore, we are forced to produce documents coming from the HVO with great difficulty and to ask witnesses at least to comment on them. As for this document, the principal interest of this document is that apart from the fact that there are at least 299 persons being under the control of the Vitez Brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, you're not answering my question. It is not to comment on the contents of the document. Do you wish this document to be authenticated by the witness; yes or no? That is the first question that you have to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interest of this document, Your Honour, is, I would say, the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I apologise for interrupting you. I'm not talking about the content of the document. Do you wish to authenticate the document as such by this witness as a document belonging to the Vitez Brigade or produced by the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not particularly to have it authenticated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, let us leave aside the authentication of the document which is contested by the Defence so that the problem of authentication is not being raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interest of the document, Your Honour, is to show that the Vitez Brigade recognised through this list that it was detaining persons. The Vitez Brigade, we have the commander of the brigade here in detention, Mario Cerkez. The interest of the document is also to show that the Muslims of Vitez were, according to the Defence, not detained or arrested but were held in various places in Vitez in order to protect them, and for the Office of the Prosecutor, it seemed of interest to produce such a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think -- we're going to go round and round on this. Look, if you want to authenticate this, you are going to have to call the Colonel back. I think that's the only way in which it can be done. If the document was given to him and it's his writing on it, then he will have to authenticate it, or if you have some other evidence on the topic. This witness clearly can't do it. He can merely identify various names. But if that's the point, to show that it's a Viteska Brigade document, and it's not accepted as such, then you're going to have, I think, to call some other evidence on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us finish with this document. The document itself cannot be tendered as a document that has been authenticated here. This does not prevent you from asking the witness about names which he may recognise or the certain number of persons on this list. It doesn't matter whether it comes from the Vitez Brigade or not but simply whether he recognises persons named on this list as prisoners held by the Vitez Brigade. That is not authenticating the document. We will, in that case, have testimony based on this list, and the basis of that testimony is something we can rely on rather than the contents of the document as such. Mr. Kovacic appears to want to add something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly and linked to what you have just said. I suggest that it should be entered in the record that the Defence is denying that this is a document issued by the Vitez Brigade. It is contesting that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think the simplest course is not to admit it in evidence, unless there's some other questions you want to ask about it, but to wait until we have the evidence on it. Do you want any more evidence about it, Mr. Lopez-Terres?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will return the document. It's ten past four. Would that be a convenient moment to adjourn?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I see there's another document coming up. Perhaps you better have a think about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. Witness AC, could you be back, please, tomorrow morning at half past nine to finish your evidence. Could you remember during this adjournment not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include members of the Prosecution. If you would be back tomorrow at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
